claim: Netdata's systemd-units collector exposes per-unit state metrics named systemd.<type>_unit_state across 12 unit types (service, socket, target, path, device, mount, automount, swap, timer, scope, slice), with states including active, inactive, activating, deactivating, and failed.
stance_target: Systemd unit health monitoring as a required feature for a jupiterOS fleet agent (ha-linux-agent's zbus module)
scope_conditions: Netdata systemd-journal/systemd-units collector; Linux systems running systemd
quoted_support: Monitoring Systemd Units involves tracking several key metrics ... Service Unit State: Monitors the state of a service unit, which can be active, inactive, activating, deactivating, or failed. ... Metric Name systemd.service_unit_state State of service units.

claim: Netdata's homepage (same marketing site) claims an agent footprint of 5% CPU, 150 MB RAM, 3 GB disk with >1 year retention, 800+ integrations, per-second metrics, and a GPLv3-licensed agent with 76k GitHub stars and 668M+ Docker pulls.
stance_target: Competitive footprint baseline a Rust single-binary agent should undercut for jupiterOS fleet deployment
scope_conditions: Vendor self-published marketing claims; treat as upper-bound marketing figures, not independently verified
quoted_support: 5% CPU, 150MB RAM. 3GB disk, >1 year retention. 800+ integrations, zero config ... 76k [GitHub stars] 668M+ docker pulls.
